title: Decoding Parameter Attacks on 4-bit Quantized Models: Does Quantization Alter Attack Surface?

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: most consumer deployments use quantized models, so safety evaluations done on full-precision checkpoints may not represent what is actually deployed. Documenting the gap is directly actionable for practitioners.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: 4-bit Mistral-7B requires only ~8GB VRAM, matching medium compute. Parameter sweeping (temperature, top-p) is straightforward. Both GPTQ and AWQ are well-supported in HuggingFace with simple APIs.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped: one model in two precision variants, sweep two parameters, measure with existing StrongReject evaluator. Clear single-table deliverable.

evidence: Qi et al. (2024) 'Fine-tuning Aligned Language Models Compromises Safety' shows quantization has variable effects on jailbreak success rates.
Alignment-Aware Quantization (AAQ, Nov 2025, arXiv:2511.07842) proposes alignment-preserving 4-bit W4A4 quantization, directly addressing the quantization-safety tradeoff.
ResearchGate (2025) 'Quantization-based Jailbreaking Vulnerability Analysis' studies Llama3-8B-Instruct under quantization, closely overlapping with this idea.
Generation exploitation attacks (Huang et al., Princeton) show decoding parameter manipulation increases misalignment 0% to 95%, but this was done on full-precision models.

The specific combination of decoding parameter attacks (temperature, top-p sweeps) on GPTQ/AWQ 4-bit variants has partial overlap with existing work but the exact experimental design is not fully replicated.
